feedback.problem:
In **ascending order,** the $x$-coordinates of the points where the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}=5$ intersects the line $y=2x$ are

$\,x=$
{{field-1}}$\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=2x,$ we first replace $y$ with $2x$ in the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} & =5 \\ \frac{(2x)^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} & =5 \\ \frac{4{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} & =5 \\ \frac{8{x}^{2}}{6}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{6} & =5 \\ \frac{5{x}^{2}}{6} & =5 \\ {x}^{2} & =6 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

So, in ascending order, the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection are
$x=-\sqrt{6}$ and $x=\sqrt{6}.$
